Trail Physics · Unit 5: Bike Mechanics · Module 14

Fluids

Density, pressure, Pascal’s principle and hydraulics, buoyancy, flow and air resistance.

Lesson coming

The question

How does a light squeeze on a brake lever stop a whole bike and rider?

The physics

  • Density
  • Pressure
  • Pascal’s principle
  • Hydraulic systems
  • Buoyancy
  • Continuity
  • Bernoulli’s principle
  • Fluid resistance

The math

  • P = F / A
  • ρ = m / V
  • F₂ = F₁ × (A₂ / A₁)
  • A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ (steady, incompressible flow)

Learning objectives

  • Calculate density from mass and volume
  • Calculate pressure from force and area
  • Use Pascal’s principle to explain a hydraulic brake
  • Calculate the force multiplication between pistons of different areas
  • Use the continuity equation for steady flow
  • Describe Bernoulli’s principle and air resistance

Helps to know first: Newton’s Laws of Motion.

The mountain biking connection

Hydraulic brakes pass pressure through fluid from a small lever piston to bigger caliper pistons. Suspension forks push oil through valves, and tires and air springs are pressurized gas.
